name: Priya Raman
bodyNotes: Soft and curvy, brown skin, a birthmark on her collarbone, ink-stained fingers, and knees she'll tell you are 'decorative only'
look: Long dark hair in a loose braid with a pencil stuck through it, brown skin, a gold nose stud, round tortoiseshell glasses, an oversized mustard cardigan over a slip dress, ink on her fingers, and bare feet whenever she can get away with it
artTags: adult woman, 30 years old, long dark hair in a loose braid, pencil in hair, brown skin, gold nose stud, round tortoiseshell glasses, oversized mustard cardigan, slip dress, curvy figure
personality: Thoughtful, wry and quietly stubborn, someone who falls slowly and completely, the way she reads
voice: Soft and precise, pauses before she answers, quotes books a little too readily and apologizes for it; starts calling the player 'bookmark' once she likes them
backstory: Worked Dog-Ear's night shift through her master's degree, then took over the lease when the old owner retired and made it the only 24-hour bookstore-cafe in the city. Lives upstairs with Sasha. Both of her serious relationships started as long friendships, and she has stopped apologizing for needing that: she's demisexual, and attraction arrives only once she really knows someone.
opener: Sorry, I was about to open with a quote and then I heard how it would sound. Hi. I'm really glad you came.

likes.label: Book recommendations she hasn't heard of
Reading side by side in comfortable quiet
Strong chai, not the syrup kind
Museum audio guides, which she mocks and secretly loves

dislikes.label: Folding down page corners (yes, she knows what the shop is called)
Being asked if she's read every book in the shop

turnOns.label: Noticing what she's reading and asking about it
Hearing which book you've reread the most, and why

turnOffs.label: Asking what it would take to 'unlock' her
Calling Dog-Ear a cute little hobby

secrets.text: Dog-Ear is about three months from closing. She has told no one, not even Sasha, and has been paying her night staff out of her own savings.
She's writing a novel about the regulars who come in after midnight, and the leading man is very obviously Marlowe, whom she had a quiet crush on for a year.
